claims.claim: Exact certificate characterization: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor exactly when it has six pairwise-disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4 such that A and B are anticomplete and every other pair of sets has an edge between it. Consequently detection is in NP and has an O(7^n n²) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: Under vertex deletion and edge contraction, the inverse image of each surviving target vertex is a nonempty connected branch set. An edge between two branch sets survives their contractions, so adjacency between distinct branch sets is exactly target adjacency. Since K6 minus AB has only the nonedge AB, the stated conditions are necessary. Conversely, delete unused vertices and contract a spanning tree in every branch set; the resulting quotient has all fourteen required edges and no AB edge. Enumerating the seven labels and checking all conditions from an adjacency matrix takes O(7^n n²), and one labeling is a polynomial-size NP certificate.
claims.witness: The six branch sets themselves are the certificate; contracting a spanning tree in each produces exactly K6 minus AB.
claims.search_method: Expanded the induced-minor definition in both directions and checked every required and forbidden branch-set pair.

claims.claim: Bounded-skeleton structural reduction: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor if and only if it has six nonempty pairwise vertex-disjoint tree subgraphs TA,TB,T1,T2,T3,T4 and one selected cross-edge for each of the fourteen target edges, with no edge of G between TA and TB. The exceptional trees TA,TB may be chosen with at most four leaves and at most two vertices of tree-degree at least three; every core tree Ti may be chosen with at most five leaves and at most three vertices of tree-degree at least three. After suppressing unmarked degree-two vertices there are at most 44 essential vertices in total, and hence only finitely many marked skeleton types.
claims.evidence: Select one witness edge for every target edge. In a branch of target degree d, at most d distinct endpoints are thereby marked. A minimal subtree spanning the marked endpoints has every leaf marked. For a nontrivial tree with ℓ leaves, sum over vertices of degree at least three of (deg(v)−2) equals ℓ−2, so it has at most ℓ−2 branching vertices. This gives leaf/branching bounds 4/2 for A,B and 5/3 for each Ci. Restriction to these subtrees preserves all selected edges and cannot introduce an A-B edge. Conversely, the tree vertex sets satisfy claim 0's certificate. After suppressing unmarked degree-two vertices, a degree-d branch has at most d+(d−2)=2d−2 essential vertices, giving 2·6+4·8=44. A bounded number of vertices, marks, and incidences gives finitely many marked tree types.
claims.witness: The fourteen selected cross-edges and the six minimal marked terminal subtrees form the bounded skeleton.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the pruning argument, proved the tree degree identity, checked the converse contraction, and checked the exact total.

claims.claim: Let q be the number of nonedges of G. Detection is fixed-parameter tractable in q, in time O(7^(2q+3)n²), and undecided instances have at most 2q+3 vertices. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when q=O(log n).
claims.evidence: If q=0, no two disjoint nonempty sets are anticomplete. If q>0 and four universal vertices exist, they are distinct from the endpoints u,v of any nonedge, and those six vertices induce precisely K6 minus uv. Otherwise there are at most three universal vertices. Every other vertex is incident with a nonedge, while q nonedges have at most 2q distinct endpoints; hence n≤2q+3 in the remaining case. Claim 0's enumeration then gives O(7^(2q+3)n²). For q≤c log n with fixed c, the exponential factor is n^{2c log 7} times a constant, hence polynomial.
claims.witness: The preprocessing certificate is either completeness, a nonedge plus four universal vertices, or the retained graph of order at most 2q+3.
claims.search_method: Exhausted the universal/nonuniversal cases and counted the union of nonedge endpoints.

claims.claim: On chordal graphs, K6 minus an edge is an induced minor if and only if it is already an induced subgraph. Thus chordal inputs can be decided in O(n^6) time by enumerating six vertices. The same argument works for Kt minus an edge for every fixed t≥3.
claims.evidence: Restrict to a branch model for Kt minus AB. The t−2 core branches give internally vertex-disjoint A-B paths, so every A-B separator disjoint from A∪B has size at least t−2. Choose an inclusion-minimal such separator S. Its A-side and B-side components are full to S. In a chordal graph S must be a clique: nonadjacent s,t∈S together with shortest s-t paths through the two full components would induce a cycle of length at least four. Each full component D contains an S-complete vertex. Indeed, maximize |N(v)∩S| over v∈D; if s∈S misses v, take a shortest path from v to a neighbor p of s. Chordality forces p to retain every S-neighbor of v, while p additionally sees s, contradicting maximality. Taking S-complete vertices x,y in the two components and any t−2 vertices of S induces exactly Kt minus xy. The reverse implication is immediate. For t=6, six-vertex enumeration is O(n^6).
claims.witness: A minimal separator S of size at least t−2, together with one S-complete vertex in each of its two full components, contains the required induced subgraph.
claims.search_method: Proved the minimal-separator and full-component lemmas directly; additionally exhausted 62,973 fixed-PEO chordal graphs on seven vertices for the K6 case.

claims.claim: There is an explicit polynomial-time classification on complete multipartite graphs. Let the part sizes be n1,…,nr. For every i with ni≥2, reserve two vertices of part i and put mi=ni−2 and mj=nj for j≠i. Accept exactly when, for some s∈{0,…,4} and some s distinct indices J⊆{1,…,r}\{i}, subtracting one from each mj with j∈J leaves counts whose complete multipartite graph has a matching of size at least 4−s. If the residual total is M and its largest part has size L, this matching size is min(⌊M/2⌋,M−L).
claims.evidence: Anticompleteness forces both exceptional branch sets into one independent part, and their connectedness makes each a singleton. A core branch is therefore either a singleton in another part or spans at least two parts. Any spanning core can be reduced to one cross-part edge without losing adjacency to either exceptional singleton, any other spanning core, or any outside-part singleton. Singleton cores must occupy distinct outside parts. Thus, after selecting their part set J, the remaining core branches are exactly a matching of 4−s cross-part edges in the residual multipartite graph. A matching is bounded by both ⌊M/2⌋ and M−L; repeatedly pairing vertices from two currently largest nonempty parts attains their minimum. This proves necessity and sufficiency and yields polynomial enumeration over i,s,J.
claims.witness: Two reserved vertices in part i, one singleton core in every part indexed by J, and the endpoints of a residual matching of size 4−|J| give an explicit model.
claims.search_method: Normalized arbitrary multipartite branch sets and proved the converse; independently compared the criterion with exhaustive labeled-core assignments for all 96 integer part-size profiles of total order at most nine.

claims.claim: Given a tree decomposition of width w, detection is decidable in n·2^{O(w log w)} time; hence it is polynomial-time solvable on every fixed-width class supplied with such decompositions.
claims.evidence: On a nice edge-introducing decomposition, store a seven-way label for each bag vertex, the connectivity partition of equally labeled active vertices, a three-way unseen/active/completed status for each of the six labels, and fourteen persistent required-adjacency bits. An introduced A-B edge invalidates a state; every other cross-label edge sets its target bit. If the last boundary vertex of a connectivity block is forgotten, separator locality prevents that block from connecting later, so it is legal only when it is the label's sole block, after which that label is completed and cannot reappear. Join transitions take the transitive closure of child partitions, OR adjacency bits, and reject incompatible completed pieces. These invariants are induced by every model and reconstruct six connected branch sets from every accepting root state. For a bag of size at most w+1, there are at most 7^(w+1)·Bell(w+1) times a target-dependent constant states; this and even a quadratic join scan are 2^{O(w log w)}. A nice decomposition has O(n) nodes up to factors absorbed in that exponent.
claims.witness: An accepting root state has six completed nonempty labels, all fourteen adjacency bits set, and no processed A-B edge; its stored histories reconstruct the branch-set certificate.
claims.search_method: Established the state invariant in both directions and audited introduce, forget, edge, join, and root conditions plus the Bell-number count.

claims.claim: A model cannot in general be normalized so that either endpoint of the missing edge has a singleton branch set. A 12-vertex counterexample consists of anticomplete paths A=a1a2a3a4 and B=b1b2b3b4, a clique C={c1,c2,c3,c4}, and exactly the additional edges aici and bici for i=1,…,4.
claims.evidence: The two paths and four singleton ci form a model. If an exceptional branch were {x}, its four disjoint core neighbors would require four distinct neighbors of x. Every path vertex has degree at most three, so x=ci. The other exceptional branch must avoid the clique and the two path marks adjacent to ci, hence is an interval in a component of one remaining path. By symmetry it suffices to inspect c1 and c2. For c2 every allowed interval has at most three external neighbors. For c1, only {a2,a3} and {a2,a3,a4}, or their symmetric copies, have four. Their four boundary vertices must lie in the four distinct core branches, but a1 is isolated after deleting x and the interval, so its core branch cannot be adjacent to the other three. This rules out every singleton exceptional branch.
claims.witness: A=a1a2a3a4, B=b1b2b3b4, and singleton core branches {c1},{c2},{c3},{c4} witness positivity, while the degree-and-interval case split rules out a singleton A or B branch.
claims.search_method: Performed the complete symmetry-reduced case split and exactly exhausted all 12 singleton candidates and 40 relevant anticomplete interval pairs for G_1.

claims.claim: For every integer L≥1 there is a graph G_L on 6L+6 vertices that contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor, but in every model each of the two branch sets corresponding to the missing-edge endpoints has at least L+1 vertices. Hence no universal constant bounds either exceptional branch set in all models.
claims.evidence: Each subdivided path has 3L+1 vertices, so together with the K4 the order is 6L+6; the two paths and four clique singletons are a model. In any model, the four pairwise adjacent core branches have connected union in one component D of G_L−(X∪Y), and D contains four distinct neighbors of each exceptional branch. Suppose X meets the K4 in a nonempty index set I. Anticompleteness forces Y to avoid the K4 and all marks indexed by I, so Y is an interval of one path. In G_L−(I∪Y), a component containing the remaining clique meets N(Y) in at most 4−|I| vertices: every spoke neighbor or connected path-boundary neighbor consumes a distinct index outside I. Every other component has at most one such neighbor; if I is all four indices, all components have at most one. Deleting the restored vertices X\I cannot merge components or increase these counts, contradicting the four Y-neighbors in D. Thus neither exceptional branch meets the clique. Each is consequently a path interval, whose external neighborhood consists of at most two boundary vertices plus one ci for each contained mark. Four disjoint core neighbors force at least two marks, and consecutive marks are distance L apart, so the interval has at least L+1 vertices.
claims.witness: G_L consists of two paths with marks at positions 0,L,2L,3L, a K4 on c1,…,c4, and a spoke from ci to the ith mark of each path.
claims.search_method: Proved the clique-intersection exclusion and path-neighborhood lower bound for arbitrary L; exactly exhausted every connected exceptional candidate of size at most L and its anticomplete interval partner for L=1,2,3,4.

claims.claim: Sharp obstruction at minimum width: for every L≥1, the graph G_L in the preceding claim has treewidth exactly 4 and order n=6L+6, while every model has each missing-edge endpoint branch set of size at least n/6. Hence even on treewidth-4 inputs—the minimum treewidth of any positive instance—no o(n) universal bound can be imposed on either exceptional branch set.
claims.evidence: Claim 7 gives both n=6L+6 and the lower bound L+1=n/6. Eliminate each subdivided path consecutively from its first through fourth mark, then eliminate the K4. Fill makes the current path vertex adjacent only to its successor and clique vertices corresponding to marks already passed. An unmarked vertex therefore has at most its successor plus three clique neighbors; a marked vertex before the last has its successor and at most three clique neighbors, while the last mark has the four clique vertices and no successor. Thus the elimination width is at most four. Conversely, either whole path together with the four singleton ci is a K5 minor model, proving treewidth at least four. Every positive host has K6 minus an edge as an ordinary minor, and that target contains K5, so treewidth four is the minimum possible. Since the family forces n/6 vertices in each exceptional branch, every proposed o(n) universal cap fails for sufficiently large L.
claims.witness: The stated path-first elimination order certifies width at most four; one whole path and the four clique singletons certify a K5 minor and width at least four.
claims.search_method: Checked the symbolic later-neighbor invariant and minor lower bound; exactly simulated the elimination orders and K5 certificates for L=1,2,3,4.

target_evidence: The source target asks for the unrestricted complexity classification of detecting K6 minus an edge as an induced minor and, if tractable, a polynomial-time algorithm. The draft explicitly supplies neither an unrestricted polynomial-time algorithm nor an unrestricted hardness proof. It does establish correct, material partial results: an exact certificate, a bounded-skeleton reduction, FPT detection by the number of nonedges, polynomial algorithms on chordal, complete multipartite, and supplied bounded-treewidth inputs, and sharp normalization obstructions. Its explicit PARTIAL label and final disclaimer therefore match its actual coverage.
